public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 347

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/347](https://www.erdosproblems.com/347)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Set Topology

namespace Erdos347

/--
The set of subset sums of a set `A ⊆ ℕ`.
-/
local notation "𝓟" A => subsetSums A

/--
Is there a sequence $A=\{a_1\leq a_2\leq \cdots\}$ of integers with
$$\lim \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}=2$$
such that
$$P(A')= \left\{\sum_{n\in B}n : B\subseteq A'\textrm{ finite }\right\}$$
has density $1$ for every cofinite subsequence $A'$ of $A$?

This has been solved in the affirmative by ebarschkis in the comments (based on idea of Tao and
van Doorn, also in the comments).

This was formalized in Lean by Barschkis using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/ebarschkis/ErdosProblem/blob/main/Problem347/Formalization.lean"]
theorem erdos_347 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, (Monotone a) ∧
      (Tendsto (fun n ↦ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∧
      (∀ ι : ℕ → ℕ, (range ι)ᶜ.Finite → HasDensity (𝓟 (range (a ∘ ι))) 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos347

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement quantifies over arbitrary maps ι : ℕ → ℕ with cofinite range, without requiring StrictMono ι, rather than explicitly quantifying over cofinite subsequences.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The condition is equivalent to density one for the subset sums of every tail. Every tail is given by a strictly increasing cofinite-range map n ↦ N + n. Conversely, every cofinite range contains a tail; subset sums are monotone under inclusion, and density one passes to supersets. Thus adding StrictMono ι changes nothing. Under the ratio-limit hypothesis, a also tends to infinity, making this equivalent to the linked proof's formulation using all S ⊆ range a with finite difference. Both equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorryAx dependencies.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a nondecreasing sequence of integers, whereas Lean uses a : ℕ → ℕ, permitting zero but excluding negative entries.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a nondecreasing integer sequence with consecutive-term ratio tending to 2, the ratio eventually exceeds 1. A negative denominator would then force a decrease, contradicting monotonicity, and a zero denominator cannot satisfy this inequality. Hence the sequence is eventually positive and strictly increasing. Taking that positive tail preserves the ratio limit and the condition on every cofinite subsequence, giving a natural-number witness. Conversely, a natural-number witness embeds into the integers; if strict positivity is required, take its eventually positive tail. The eventual-positivity assertions were proved in Lean, but the complete integer/natural existence equivalence was not formalized.
